- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2 days above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model overestimates recovery; shift forecast downward by 3–5% for next 5 days.  
- Model often underestimates mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- If forecast is significantly above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 2–4% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model may misread momentum; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in sentiment effect.
